intent: Split setup_dns_blocker.sh under the cap without disturbing the live systemd unit that runs it.
changes: Three libs: the dnsmasq config and systemd unit writers, the validation and firewall block, and the DHCP-server and status block. All seven heredocs sit inside functions, so function boundaries were safe seams.
The script guards its own entry with SETUP_DNS_BLOCKER_SKIP_MAIN, which made a proper function-set comparison possible on a script that otherwise reconfigures the machine when sourced.

verification.command: SETUP_DNS_BLOCKER_SKIP_MAIN=1 source the script and diff `declare -F` against a detached worktree at HEAD
verification.evidence: Identical 74-function set (its own plus common.sh's). This is the same check used for the two shared libs, and it is available here only because the script provides that escape hatch.

verification.command: systemctl cat dns-blocklist-refresh.service, test -f its ExecStart, bash -n that file
verification.evidence: Still resolves to the split script and still parses. This is one of only two units pointing into the repo.

verification.command: bash -n on the entry and each lib; pre-commit run --files
verification.evidence: All four parse and the gate is clean, with no suppression.

risks: main() was not run: it installs dnsmasq, writes units, and changes nftables and DHCP settings on the live LAN. The function-set diff proves the surface, not the behaviour.
The refresh timer invokes the script with `refresh`, which reaches cmd_refresh through the same dispatch; that path is covered by the function-set check but not executed.
rollback: git revert the commit; the script returns to 569 lines and the three libs disappear.
After rollback, re-run the SKIP_MAIN function-set check and expect the same 74 names.
